scope: shift strategy: replay a real gamestate body from our own server instead of reverse-engineering the 2697 key stream

key_realization.insight: we do not need to reproduce the 2697 command string at all: our own server can keep lastClientCommandString empty, which makes the cipher key constant per packet (challenge ^ seq)
key_realization.why_it_works: the client's decoder uses the same formula the server's encoder used, so a constant key on our side is decoded correctly by the client
key_realization.consequence: the whole key-shift problem becomes irrelevant for our own outbound path

implementation.gamestate_plaintext_loader: _load_gamestate_plaintext() decrypts runs/final-in.jsonl with the recorded challenge and returns the 1168-byte body
implementation.outbound: packet = seq(4) + xor(plaintext, challenge ^ seq); the command string is empty by design

known_defect.issue: the first ten bytes of the recovered plaintext are still 8b-prefixed, i.e. contaminated by the 2697 command-stream key shift that we could not reproduce
known_defect.impact: if replayed verbatim, the client would see a garbled header before the valid mp_cross_fire configstring
known_defect.fix: replace those leading bytes with a correct gamestate header before sending

next: determine the correct 15-byte header (map name sits at offset 15 in the recovered plaintext, so the header is exactly that long)
candidate header from the source write order with the 2697-contaminated bytes removed: lastClientCommand(4) + svc_EOF(1) + 0(4) + svc_gamestate(4) + ... trimmed to 15 bytes
emit seq + xor(header + rest_of_plaintext_from_offset_15, challenge ^ seq) and watch the client
